details : - snapshot model : redwood uses a chained incremental snapshot model. each incremental references blocks / chunks from previous snapshots. deleting a volume / object creates a logical tombstone ; subsequent gc marks unreachable chunks. we keep chunks until all references expire or until retention / expunge is triggered. - tombstones vs physical expunge : tombstones are immediate ( logical deletion ) for metadata, which removes the object from active listing and apis. physical data removal is asynchronous to allow safe restores and to support point - in - time recovery. - retention and gc windows : there are two configurable values that determine the effective expunge timeline : * retention _ ttl ( set by customer )

{
  "document": {
    "id": "dsid_d7f999ad71f145a09f290ad23190df8b",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides/private-deploy-operational-hardening-and-safe-migration-playbook-2026.json",
    "title": "Operational Hardening and Safe Migration Playbook for Private Deploys",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Operational Hardening and Safe Migration Playbook for Private Deploys\",\n  \"space\": \"eng-private-deployments\",\n  \"author\": \"Emma Chen\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-02-10\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2026-09-01\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Diego Morales\",\n    \"Aisha Patel\",\n    \"Lena Hoffman\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"private-deploy\",\n    \"migration\",\n    \"runbook\",\n    \"telemetry\",\n    \"rollback\",\n    \"hardening\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"internal\",\n  \"content\": \"Summary:\\\\nThis playbook describes an engineering-first process for operational hardening and safe workload migration for Redwood Private deployments (VPC and on-prem bundles). It combines pre-migration verification, staged rollout guidance, continuous telemetry checks, and a deterministic rollback matrix to minimize customer downtime and data risk during model, runtime, or infra migrations.\\\\n\\\\nScope and audience:\\\\n- Scope: Private deployments delivered via Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem) including model swaps, runtime upgrades, kernel/quantization changes, and capacity migration between pools.\\\\n- Audience: Field engineers, SREs, deployment engineers, solutions architects, and customer success leads supporting private customers.\\\\n\\\\nOwner and escalation:\\\\n- Primary owner: Private Deployments Team (eng-private-deployments).\\\\n- Runbook owner: Emma Chen (Runbook maintainer).\\\\n- On-call escalation: Private-deploys oncall -> Eng SRE -> Platform Lead.\\\\n\\\\nSuccess criteria and SLOs for migration activity:\\\\n- Migration must not exceed 2x historical 1h error rate at 95th percentile for production traffic during the 30-minute canary window.\\\\n- Mean token latency must not regress by more than 15% from baseline across 99th percentile after steady-state (1 hour).\\\\n- No data-loss incidents (0 lost requests) and KV/embedding cache semantics preserved.\\\\n\\\\nPrerequisites checklist (must be green before starting):\\\\n| Item | Description | Owner | Required state |\\\\n|---|---|---|---|\\\\n| Customer readiness call | Confirm maintenance window and rollback authority | Solutions Eng | scheduled/acknowledged |\\\\n| Backups | Snapshot model artifacts, KV cache snapshot if stateful | Field Engineer | completed |\\\\n| Telemetry hooks | Ensure sampling rules and traces are enabled at 100% for canary nodes | SRE | enabled |\\\\n| Capacity reserve | 20% spare GPU headroom in same region or burst pool | Capacity Planner | verified |\\\\n| Access | Field engineer has customer admin KMS & SSH keys (if onprem) | Field Engineer | verified |\\\\n\\\\nPre-migration validation (pre-flight):\\\\n1) Inventory and compatibility matrix\\\\n- Validate model binary ABI, quantization profile, and kernel compatibility against runtime version using the compatibility-checker tool:\\\\n  - CLI: rdx-compat-check --model <MODEL_PATH> --runtime <RUNTIME_TAG> --output summary.json\\\\n  - Expected exit 0. Attach summary.json to migration ticket.\\\\n2) Smoke harness in staging mirror\\\\n- Deploy identical staging shard with 10% representative KV sizes, and run the canonical smoke set (prompt-shard-smoke.json) for 30 minutes.\\\\n3) Telemetry assertion baseline\\\\n- Collect 1h of baseline telemetry (latency percentiles, error rates, token generation rate) and store in migration-buffer: bucket://redwood-migrations/<customer>/<migration-id>/baseline.json\\\\n\\\\nStaged rollout plan (recommended):\\\\n- Phase 0: Dry-run verify (no traffic) \\u2014 deploy to a single node in the staging cluster and run smoke tests (20\\u201330 minutes).\\\\n- Phase 1: Canary (1\\u20133% traffic) \\u2014 route a small percentage of production traffic to new runtime/model variant for 30 minutes. Use runtime routing policy: ROUTE_POLICY=migration-canary-<id>.\\\\n- Phase 2: Ramp (5\\u201325%) \\u2014 4 sequential ramps (5, 10, 15, 25%) each with a 15\\u201330 minute observation window.\\\\n- Phase 3: Partial production (50%) \\u2014 if all metrics stable, move to 50% for 30\\u201360 minutes with full end-to-end smoke across customer flows.\\\\n- Phase 4: Full cutover (100%) \\u2014 proceed only after green across all checks for at least 1 hour.\\\\n\\\\nMetric checks and automated abort criteria (each check evaluated continuously during windows):\\\\n- Error rate (5xx) must not exceed baseline*2 for canary window or baseline + 1% absolute for larger ramps.\\\\n- Latency: P99 token latency regression >15% triggers abort.\\\\n- Quality guardrails: Automated evals on canonical prompts must not drop top-1 semantic score by >6 points (or configured customer threshold).\\\\n- Resource saturation: GPU memory usage >90% or CPU steal >40% triggers abort and immediate rollback.\\\\n- Request failure modes: Increase in KV cache misses >2x baseline -> investigate, hold ramp.\\\\n\\\\nRollback matrix (deterministic mapping of failure mode -> rollback action):\\\\n- Failure: P99 latency regression >15% during any window -> Action: Immediate route revert to prior variant, scale new nodes to 0, alert SRE and field engineer.\\\\n- Failure: Error rate >2x baseline in canary -> Action: Pause routing, scale down canary nodes, run 'rdx-dump-logs' and gather stack traces.\\\\n- Failure: Quality regression detected on canonical evals -> Action: Stop ramp, close canary, replace candidate model with previous build; if quick fix unavailable, rollback.\\\\n- Failure: KMS access error for decryption of model weights -> Action: Revoke new deployment, rollback and coordinate with security/KMS owner.\\\\n\\\\nImmediate rollback commands (examples):\\\\n- API rollback (hosted control plane cooperating with private control plane):\\\\n  - curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>' \\\\\\\\n    https://private-control.<customer>.redwood/api/v1/rollouts/<migration-id>/rollback\\\\n- On-prem operator (kubectl example):\\\\n  - kubectl -n redwood set image deploy/runtime runtime=redwood/runtime:<previous-tag> --record\\\\n  - kubectl rollout status deploy/runtime -n redwood --timeout=10m\\\\n\\\\nPost-rollback triage checklist:\\\\n1) Capture telemetry from rollback window and retain for 30 days in migration bucket.\\\\n2) Open a detailed incident record with root cause hypothesis within 24 hours.\\\\n3) Schedule a fix/patch release or adjust config and re-run a scheduled test migration in staging.\\\\n\\\\nDay-2 operational hardening tasks (post-cutover):\\\\n- Config hardening: Enforce CIS-like kernel tuning for onprem images (sysctl settings) \\u2014 include the sample sysctl block below in the node bootstrap:\\\\n  - net.core.somaxconn=1024\\\\n  - vm.swappiness=10\\\\n  - vm.dirty_ratio=15\\\\n- Token sampling & traces: Maintain 10% request trace sampling for first 72 hours, then drop to customer agreed sampling (default 1%).\\\\n- Log retention: Increase debug-level retention for migration nodes to 168 hours (7 days) and route to customer-owned S3 for audit.\\\\n\\\\nTelemetry and acceptance checks (post-cutover steady-state):\\\\n- Validation run (24h): Run full acceptance harness that includes throughput, latency, and guardrail checks.\\\\n- Customer smoke test: Coordinate with customer success to validate critical flows using the customer acceptance test suite.\\\\n- Drift detection: Run nightly compare of embedding distribution, per-prompt generation length, and tokenization diffs for first 72 hours.\\\\n\\\\nPackaging and artifact concerns:\\\\n- Model artifact immutability: Tag artifacts with semantic version + digest (e.g., model-v1.4+sha256:abc123). The runtime only pulls artifacts that match digest.\\\\n- Image signing: All runtime images for production use must be signed with internal cosign keys. Verification command example: cosign verify --key /secure/keys/cosign.pub <image>.\\\\n\\\\nRisk matrix (summary):\\\\n- High risk: Stateful cache mismatch, KMS decryption errors, embedded token loss during migration. Mitigation: snapshots, dry-run with representative KV sizes, pre-checks for KMS policies.\\\\n- Medium risk: Performance regressions due to kernel selection or quantization. Mitigation: compat-checker, small density canaries, telemetry thresholds.\\\\n- Low risk: Observability gaps; mitigated by pre-enabling traces and temporary elevated sampling.\\\\n\\\\nOperational play examples (snippets):\\\\n- Sample alert policy (Pseudo):\\\\n  - alert: Migration_P99_Latency_Regression\\\\n    expr: (migration_p99_latency / baseline_p99_latency) > 1.15\\\\n    for: 5m\\\\n    labels: { severity: page }\\\\n\\\\n- Minimal acceptance smoke curl test:\\\\n  - curl -X POST https://private-api.customer.example/v1/generate \\\\\\\\n    -H \\\\\\\"Authorization: Bearer <token>\\\\\\\" \\\\\\\\n    -H \\\\\\\"Content-Type: application/json\\\\\\\" \\\\\\\\n    -d '{\\\"model\\\":\\\"<candidate>\\\",\\\"prompt\\\":\\\"Hello world\\\",\\\"max_tokens\\\":16}'\\\\n\\\\nRelated pages and artifacts to attach before starting:\\\\n- Link: continuous improvement:\\\\n- After any migration that required rollback or exceeded thresholds, run a 72-hour retrospective including: timeline, telemetry snapshots, root cause, corrective actions, and a retro ticket with owner and target fix date.\\\\n\\\\nAppendix A \\u2014 Quick reference commands:\\\\n- rdx-compat-check --model /artifacts/model.tar.gz --runtime runtime:2026-02-01 --output       "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Operational Hardening and Safe Migration Playbook for Private Deploys\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides/private-deploy-operational-hardening-and-safe-migration-playbook-2026.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: eng-private-deployments\n\ncontent : summary : \\ nthis playbook describes an engineering - first process for operational hardening and safe workload migration for redwood private deployments ( vpc and on - prem bundles ). it combines pre - migration verification, staged rollout guidance, continuous telemetry checks, and a deterministic rollback matrix to minimize customer downtime and data risk during model, runtime, or infra migrations. \\ n \\ nscope and audience : \\ n - scope : private deployments delivered via redwood private ( vpc and on - prem ) including model swaps, runtime upgrades, kernel / quantization changes, and capacity migration between pools. \\ n - audience : field engineers, sres, deployment engineers, solutions architects, and customer success leads supporting private customers",

document.title: Operational Hardening and Safe Migration Playbook for Private Deploys
document.content:
{
  "title": "Operational Hardening and Safe Migration Playbook for Private Deploys",
  "space": "eng-private-deployments",
  "author": "Emma Chen",
  "owner_team": "engineering",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2026-02-10",
  "last_updated": "2026-09-01",
  "reviewers": [
    "Diego Morales",
    "Aisha Patel",
    "Lena Hoffman"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "private-deploy",
    "migration",
    "runbook",
    "telemetry",
    "rollback",
    "hardening"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "content": "Summary:\\nThis playbook describes an engineering-first process for operational hardening and safe workload migration for Redwood Private deployments (VPC and on-prem bundles). It combines pre-migration verification, staged rollout guidance, continuous telemetry checks, and a deterministic rollback matrix to minimize customer downtime and data risk during model, runtime, or infra migrations.\\n\\nScope and audience:\\n- Scope: Private deployments delivered via Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem) including model swaps, runtime upgrades, kernel/quantization changes, and capacity migration between pools.\\n- Audience: Field engineers, SREs, deployment engineers, solutions architects, and customer success leads supporting private customers.\\n\\nOwner and escalation:\\n- Primary owner: Private Deployments Team (eng-private-deployments).\\n- Runbook owner: Emma Chen (Runbook maintainer).\\n- On-call escalation: Private-deploys oncall -> Eng SRE -> Platform Lead.\\n\\nSuccess criteria and SLOs for migration activity:\\n- Migration must not exceed 2x historical 1h error rate at 95th percentile for production traffic during the 30-minute canary window.\\n- Mean token latency must not regress by more than 15% from baseline across 99th percentile after steady-state (1 hour).\\n- No data-loss incidents (0 lost requests) and KV/embedding cache semantics preserved.\\n\\nPrerequisites checklist (must be green before starting):\\n| Item | Description | Owner | Required state |\\n|---|---|---|---|\\n| Customer readiness call | Confirm maintenance window and rollback authority | Solutions Eng | scheduled/acknowledged |\\n| Backups | Snapshot model artifacts, KV cache snapshot if stateful | Field Engineer | completed |\\n| Telemetry hooks | Ensure sampling rules and traces are enabled at 100% for canary nodes | SRE | enabled |\\n| Capacity reserve | 20% spare GPU headroom in same region or burst pool | Capacity Planner | verified |\\n| Access | Field engineer has customer admin KMS & SSH keys (if onprem) | Field Engineer | verified |\\n\\nPre-migration validation (pre-flight):\\n1) Inventory and compatibility matrix\\n- Validate model binary ABI, quantization profile, and kernel compatibility against runtime version using the compatibility-checker tool:\\n  - CLI: rdx-compat-check --model <MODEL_PATH> --runtime <RUNTIME_TAG> --output summary.json\\n  - Expected exit 0. Attach summary.json to migration ticket.\\n2) Smoke harness in staging mirror\\n- Deploy identical staging shard with 10% representative KV sizes, and run the canonical smoke set (prompt-shard-smoke.json) for 30 minutes.\\n3) Telemetry assertion baseline\\n- Collect 1h of baseline telemetry (latency percentiles, error rates, token generation rate) and store in migration-buffer: bucket://redwood-migrations/<customer>/<migration-id>/baseline.json\\n\\nStaged rollout plan (recommended):\\n- Phase 0: Dry-run verify (no traffic) \u2014 deploy to a single node in the staging cluster and run smoke tests (20\u201330 minutes).\\n- Phase 1: Canary (1\u20133% traffic) \u2014 route a small percentage of production traffic to new runtime/model variant for 30 minutes. Use runtime routing policy: ROUTE_POLICY=migration-canary-<id>.\\n- Phase 2: Ramp (5\u201325%) \u2014 4 sequential ramps (5, 10, 15, 25%) each with a 15\u201330 minute observation window.\\n- Phase 3: Partial production (50%) \u2014 if all metrics stable, move to 50% for 30\u201360 minutes with full end-to-end smoke across customer flows.\\n- Phase 4: Full cutover (100%) \u2014 proceed only after green across all checks for at least 1 hour.\\n\\nMetric checks and automated abort criteria (each check evaluated continuously during windows):\\n- Error rate (5xx) must not exceed baseline*2 for canary window or baseline + 1% absolute for larger ramps.\\n- Latency: P99 token latency regression >15% triggers abort.\\n- Quality guardrails: Automated evals on canonical prompts must not drop top-1 semantic score by >6 points (or configured customer threshold).\\n- Resource saturation: GPU memory usage >90% or CPU steal >40% triggers abort and immediate rollback.\\n- Request failure modes: Increase in KV cache misses >2x baseline -> investigate, hold ramp.\\n\\nRollback matrix (deterministic mapping of failure mode -> rollback action):\\n- Failure: P99 latency regression >15% during any window -> Action: Immediate route revert to prior variant, scale new nodes to 0, alert SRE and field engineer.\\n- Failure: Error rate >2x baseline in canary -> Action: Pause routing, scale down canary nodes, run 'rdx-dump-logs' and gather stack traces.\\n- Failure: Quality regression detected on canonical evals -> Action: Stop ramp, close canary, replace candidate model with previous build; if quick fix unavailable, rollback.\\n- Failure: KMS access error for decryption of model weights -> Action: Revoke new deployment, rollback and coordinate with security/KMS owner.\\n\\nImmediate rollback commands (examples):\\n- API rollback (hosted control plane cooperating with private control plane):\\n  - curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>' \\\\n    https://private-control.<customer>.redwood/api/v1/rollouts/<migration-id>/rollback\\n- On-prem operator (kubectl example):\\n  - kubectl -n redwood set image deploy/runtime runtime=redwood/runtime:<previous-tag> --record\\n  - kubectl rollout status deploy/runtime -n redwood --timeout=10m\\n\\nPost-rollback triage checklist:\\n1) Capture telemetry from rollback window and retain for 30 days in migration bucket.\\n2) Open a detailed incident record with root cause hypothesis within 24 hours.\\n3) Schedule a fix/patch release or adjust config and re-run a scheduled test migration in staging.\\n\\nDay-2 operational hardening tasks (post-cutover):\\n- Config hardening: Enforce CIS-like kernel tuning for onprem images (sysctl settings) \u2014 include the sample sysctl block below in the node bootstrap:\\n  - net.core.somaxconn=1024\\n  - vm.swappiness=10\\n  - vm.dirty_ratio=15\\n- Token sampling & traces: Maintain 10% request trace sampling for first 72 hours, then drop to customer agreed sampling (default 1%).\\n- Log retention: Increase debug-level retention for migration nodes to 168 hours (7 days) and route to customer-owned S3 for audit.\\n\\nTelemetry and acceptance checks (post-cutover steady-state):\\n- Validation run (24h): Run full acceptance harness that includes throughput, latency, and guardrail checks.\\n- Customer smoke test: Coordinate with customer success to validate critical flows using the customer acceptance test suite.\\n- Drift detection: Run nightly compare of embedding distribution, per-prompt generation length, and tokenization diffs for first 72 hours.\\n\\nPackaging and artifact concerns:\\n- Model artifact immutability: Tag artifacts with semantic version + digest (e.g., model-v1.4+sha256:abc123). The runtime only pulls artifacts that match digest.\\n- Image signing: All runtime images for production use must be signed with internal cosign keys. Verification command example: cosign verify --key /secure/keys/cosign.pub <image>.\\n\\nRisk matrix (summary):\\n- High risk: Stateful cache mismatch, KMS decryption errors, embedded token loss during migration. Mitigation: snapshots, dry-run with representative KV sizes, pre-checks for KMS policies.\\n- Medium risk: Performance regressions due to kernel selection or quantization. Mitigation: compat-checker, small density canaries, telemetry thresholds.\\n- Low risk: Observability gaps; mitigated by pre-enabling traces and temporary elevated sampling.\\n\\nOperational play examples (snippets):\\n- Sample alert policy (Pseudo):\\n  - alert: Migration_P99_Latency_Regression\\n    expr: (migration_p99_latency / baseline_p99_latency) > 1.15\\n    for: 5m\\n    labels: { severity: page }\\n\\n- Minimal acceptance smoke curl test:\\n  - curl -X POST https://private-api.customer.example/v1/generate \\\\n    -H \\\"Authorization: Bearer <token>\\\" \\\\n    -H \\\"Content-Type: application/json\\\" \\\\n    -d '{\"model\":\"<candidate>\",\"prompt\":\"Hello world\",\"max_tokens\":16}'\\n\\nRelated pages and artifacts to attach before starting:\\n- Link: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides/private-deploy-onboarding-and-failover-runbook-2026 (onboarding checklist)\\n- Link: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/post-installation-telemetry-and-acceptance-checklist-2026 (telemetry norms)\\n- Artifact: compatibility-checker summary.json\\n\\nPost-mortem and continuous improvement:\\n- After any migration that required rollback or exceeded thresholds, run a 72-hour retrospective including: timeline, telemetry snapshots, root cause, corrective actions, and a retro ticket with owner and target fix date.\\n\\nAppendix A \u2014 Quick reference commands:\\n- rdx-compat-check --model /artifacts/model.tar.gz --runtime runtime:2026-02-01 --output /tmp/compat.json\\n- rdx-deploy --bundle /artifacts/private-bundle.tar.gz --target canary-node --annotations migration-id=<id>\\n- rdx-metrics tail --window 30m --filter migration=<id>\\n\\nAppendix B \u2014 Minimal staging smoke suite (file: prompt-shard-smoke.json)\\n- [\\n  { \\\"prompt\\\": \\\"Summarize the following text in one sentence:\\\" },\\n  { \\\"prompt\\\": \\\"Extract the product name from: 'Order 9382: Redwood Tuner'\\\" },\\n  { \\\"prompt\\\": \\\"Rewrite for clarity: 'Received bad kernel selection leading to slow tokens'\\\" }\\n]\\n\\nContact and support:\\n- Private Deployments Team Slack: #private-deploys\\n- On-call pager: +1-650-555-0110 (internal)\\n- Field sales/customer success contact: see migration ticket metadata\\n\\nChange log:\\n- 2026-02-10 \u2014 created by Emma Chen (initial draft).\\n- 2026-04-12 \u2014 added deterministic rollback matrix and KMS checks (review by Diego Morales).\\n- 2026-09-01 \u2014 clarified telemetry windows and added example cosign verify step (review by Aisha Patel).\\n",
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "content"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_d7f999ad71f145a09f290ad23190df8b"
}

    "title": "Failure Isolation and Rollback Playbook for Private Deployments",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Failure Isolation and Rollback Playbook for Private Deployments\",\n  \"space\": \"eng-private-deployments\",\n  \"author\": \"Aisha Khan\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-02-12\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2026-03-01\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Marco Perez\",\n    \"Samantha Lee\",\n    \"Darren O'Neill\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"rollback\",\n    \"on-prem\",\n    \"vpc\",\n    \"runbook\",\n    \"day2\",\n    \"slo\"\n  ],\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"/confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides/private-deploy-playbook-vpc-onprem-2026\",\n    \"/confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/onprem-vpc-day2-automation-and-upgrade-playbook-2025\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"restricted\",\n  \"body\": \"Summary:\\n\\nThis playbook describes failure isolation patterns, safe rollback procedures, verification checks, and communication steps for Redwood Private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It is intended for SREs, Platform engineers, and Customer Success engineers who run day-2 operations or perform upgrades/patches that risk degrading service availability, security posture, or data integrity.\\n\\nGoals:\\n- Minimize customer-visible disruption during upgrades and incidents.\\n- Ensure safe automated and manual rollback paths exist for all control-plane and data-plane changes.\\n- Provide clear ownership, decision criteria, and verification checks for rollback decisions.\\n\\nScope and applicability:\\n- Applies to: Redwood Private control plane, connector agents, inference runtime nodes, KV/cache tiers, and networking changes introduced during patch/upgrade or configuration rollout.\\n- Does NOT cover: customer-managed external dependencies (e.g., third-party DBs) except where Redwood config changes interact directly.\\n\\nPreconditions (must-check before any planned upgrade):\\n1) Backups & snapshots: confirm last full control-plane snapshot is completed and stored in the configured customer bucket. Snapshot timestamp: <ISO timestamp>.\\n2) Health baseline: capture baseline metrics for 15 min prior to change (latency p95, CPU/GPU utilization, request success rate, cache hit rate). Attach reports to the change ticket.\\n3) Canary capacity: allocate a canary pool with isolated routing (>=1% traffic and at least N concurrent sessions, where N = max(10, 0.01 * expected concurrent load)).\\n4) Rollback playbook verified: owners and on-call contact listed in the change ticket.\\n\\nKey failure-isolation patterns (design rules):\\n- Traffic fencing: use route-level flags and feature gates so new binaries/configs can be routed only from an explicit routing table entry.\\n- Config gating: store critical rollout knobs in the control-plane feature collection; changes to these keys must be reversible and have a TTL.\\n- Immutable artifacts: build deterministic artifacts (sha256). If artifact mismatch occurs, auto-reject rollout.\\n- Gradual widening: 0 -> canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated health gates at each step.\\n\\nDecision criteria for rollback (one or more triggers):\\n- Latency: sustained p95 increase > 2x baseline for 5 minutes.\\n- Errors: request error rate increase > 1% absolute and >= 3x baseline for 3 minutes.\\n- Throughput degradation: end-to-end throughput drop > 20% for 5 minutes with no external cause.\\n- Resource saturation: any node with GPU memory OOM, kernel panic, repeated process restarts (>3 restarts in 5 minutes).\\n- Security regression: any failing auth or encryption checks during/after rollout.\\n\\nRecommended manual rollback procedure (control-plane or runtime service):\\n1) Triage and verify: confirm metrics trigger was real (check Prometheus, traces, and node logs). Record decision in the incident/change ticket.\\n2) Stop new widening: set rollout flag to paused.\\n3) Shift traffic: route 100% traffic away from canary/widened group to last-known-good pool. Use routing command: \\n   rwd-router set-route --deployment <DEPLOYMENT_ID> --target-pool <GOOD_POOL_ID> --drain-time 30s\\n4) If traffic cannot be re-routed cleanly, place a temporary denylist for new sessions at the gateway: \\n   rwd-gateway denylist add --match \\\"session=new\\\" --reason \\\"rollback in progress\\\"\\n5) Revert artifacts: pin model/runtime to previous artifact SHA. Example pin file (used by control-plane):\\n\\n   pinned_artifact: >\\n     deployment: infra-runtime\\n     version: 2026.01.14\\n     sha256: abcd1234ef567890...\\n\\n   Apply revert command: rwd-deploy rollback --deployment infra-runtime --to-sha abcd1234ef567890 --force\\n\\n6) Rollback config: restore previous config bundle from snapshot store. Example restore: rwd-config restore --snapshot-id snap-20260210-2145 --components control-plane,runtime\\n7) Verify service health: follow verification checklist below.\\n8) Close ticket with a post-rollback summary including root cause hypothesis and actions to mitigate in next rollout.\\n\\nAutomated rollback choreography (when health gates are enabled):\\n- Health gate engine monitors: p95 latency, error rate, GPU OOM rate, and control-plane heartbeat.\\n- If any configured gate trips, the system will attempt: 1) pause widen, 2) move traffic back to the last good pool, 3) notify on-call channel, 4) if critical triggers persist for 90s, automatically initiate artifact revert.\\n- To disable automated rollback for a specific rollout, add hold tag: rollout.hold=true in the change request (not recommended unless supervised).\\n\\nVerification checklist (post-rollback):\\n- Control-plane: api-server 200s check, queue depth stable, config hash matches pinned SHA.\\n- Runtime: no GPU OOMs for 30 minutes, tail latency p50/p95 within 15% of baseline.\\n- Workloads: 10 synthetic requests per model class succeed end-to-end, embeddings within expected vector L2 tolerance.\\n- Logs: no new error patterns (>5 occurrences) in last 15 minutes.\\n- Security: TLS session negotiation passes, KMS sign/verify checks succeed.\\n\\nConcrete commands and examples (CLI snippets):\\n- Snapshot control plane:\\n  rwd-control snapshot create --name pre-upgrade-2026-02-12\\n\\n- Create canary pool (example YAML passed to control-plane API):\\n  ```yaml\\n  kind: Pool\\n  name: canary-2026-02-12\\n  labels:\\n    purpose: canary\\n    owner: eng-platform\\n  size: 4\\n  allowed_models: [rwd-gpt-small, rwd-gpt-medium]\\n  ```\\n\\n- Trigger manual rollback for runtime:\\n  rwd-deploy rollback --deployment inference-runtime --reason \\\"p95 spike\\\" --to-tag last-good\\n\\n- Inspect recent errors (Kubernetes example):\\n  kubectl -n rwd-runtime logs deployment/inference-runtime --since=15m | grep -i error | head -n 200\\n\\nOperational notes and edge cases:\\n- Database schema incompatible migrations: never auto-rollback schema changes. For schema rollouts, use migration gating and a multi-step backward-compatible migration plan. If a schema incompatibility is detected, trigger service-level rollback but coordinate with DBA team to run the corrective migration.\\n- Persistent data corruption suspected: isolate affected nodes immediately, take disk snapshots, and contact Security for potential forensics. Do NOT reintroduce those nodes into the pool.\\n- Multi-region fallbacks: if local region capacity causes rollback, prefer moving traffic to a warm spare region with identical model versions. Ensure legal/data-residency approvals before cross-region movement.\\n\\nPost-incident actions and ownership:\\n- Postmortem owner: on-call engineer who initiated rollback (or explicit postmortem owner in ticket).\\n- RCA timeline: initial report due within 2 business days, full RCA with action items within 7 business days.\\n- Preventative controls: implement additional health gates, add synthetic tests, or modify resource requests based on root cause.\\n\\nCompatibility and upgrade matrix (excerpt):\\n- Control plane version 2025.12.x: compatible with runtime 2025.10.x -> 2026.01.x (recommended).\\n- Runtime GPU driver: NVIDIA 535.x required for 16-bit quantized kernels.\\n- KV cache format v2 requires control-plane >=2026.01.\\n\\nSafety checklist before re-attempting rollout:\\n1) Confirm root cause has been mitigated or a compensating control exists.\\n2) Increase canary pool size by 2x and reduce widening step to 5% increments.\\n3) Add extra synthetic probes and extend observation window to 30 minutes between steps.\\n4) Ensure on-call rotation for the next 48 hours has explicit coverage.\\n\\nTroubleshooting quick reference (common scenarios):\\n- Symptom: p95 doubled immediately after rollout. Check: network egress throttling on gateway, routing misconfiguration, and runtime CPU throttling. Action: move traffic and revert.\\n- Symptom: GPU OOM on new model. Check: model quantization profile, batch size defaults. Action: rollback to previous model; file model-onboarding ticket.\\n\\nAppendix A \\u2014 Minimal set of monitoring queries to attach to the change ticket:\\n- PromQL p95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[1m])) by (le, route))\\n- Error rate: sum(rate(request_errors_total[1m])) / sum(rate(request_total[1m]))\\n- Node restarts: increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total[5m]) > 0\\n\\nAppendix B \\u2014 Contact & escalation matrix:\\n- Primary on-call (Platform SRE): pager duty rotation rwd-platform-pager (escalate after 5 min)\\n- Control-plane owner: eng-platform@redwood.example.com\\n- Security: sec-ops@redwood.example.com (for suspected compromise)\\n\\nDocument maintenance:\\n- Owner: eng-platform\\n- Review cadence: quarterly or after any major rollback incident\\n- Last reviewed by: Marco Perez on 2026-03-01\\n\\nRelated artifacts and links:\\n- Pre-rollout checklist template: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/templates/pre-rollout-checklist\\n- Canary dashboard: /dashboards/canary-health\\n\\nEnd of document.\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"body\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_fb0f5bcf6911468b8787ee48d1bef44a\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Failure Isolation and Rollback Playbook for Private Deployments\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/private-deploy-failure-isolation-rollback-playbook-2026.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: eng-private-deployments\n\n##c - day2 - automation - and - upgrade - playbook - 2025 confidentiality : restricted body : summary : this playbook describes failure isolation patterns, safe rollback procedures, verification checks, and communication steps for redwood private deployments ( vpc and on - prem ). it is intended for sres, platform engineers, and customer success engineers who run day - 2 operations or perform upgrades / patches that risk degrading service availability, security posture, or data integrity. goals : - minimize customer - visible disruption during upgrades and incidents. - ensure safe automated and manual rollback paths exist for all control - plane and data - plane changes. - provide clear ownership, decision criteria, and verification checks for rollback decisions.",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Failure Isolation and Rollback Playbook for Private Deployments\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/private-deploy-failure-isolation-rollback-playbook-2026.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: eng-private-deployments\n\n0 - > canary - > 10 % - > 50 % - > 100 % with automated health gates at each step. decision criteria for rollback ( one or more triggers ) : - latency : sustained p95 increase > 2x baseline for 5 minutes. - errors : request error rate increase > 1 % absolute and > = 3x baseline for 3 minutes. - throughput degradation : end - to - end throughput drop > 20 % for 5 minutes with no external cause. - resource saturation : any node with gpu memory oom, kernel panic, repeated process restarts ( > 3 restarts in 5 minutes ). - security regression : any failing auth or encryption checks during / after rollout.",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Failure Isolation and Rollback Playbook for Private Deployments\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/private-deploy-failure-isolation-rollback-playbook-2026.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: eng-private-deployments\n\n) close ticket with a post - rollback summary including root cause hypothesis and actions to mitigate in next rollout. automated rollback choreography ( when health gates are enabled ) : - health gate engine monitors : p95 latency, error rate, gpu oom rate, and control - plane heartbeat. - if any configured gate trips, the system will attempt : 1 ) pause widen, 2 ) move traffic back to the last good pool, 3 ) notify on - call channel, 4 ) if critical triggers persist for 90s, automatically initiate artifact revert. - to disable automated rollback for a specific rollout, add hold tag : rollout. hold = true in the change request ( not recommended unless supervised ).",

  ],
  "confidentiality": "restricted",
  "body": "Summary:

This playbook describes failure isolation patterns, safe rollback procedures, verification checks, and communication steps for Redwood Private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It is intended for SREs, Platform engineers, and Customer Success engineers who run day-2 operations or perform upgrades/patches that risk degrading service availability, security posture, or data integrity.

Goals:
- Minimize customer-visible disruption during upgrades and incidents.
- Ensure safe automated and manual rollback paths exist for all control-plane and data-plane changes.
- Provide clear ownership, decision criteria, and verification checks for rollback decisions.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to: Redwood Private control plane, connector agents, inference runtime nodes, KV/cache tiers, and networking changes introduced during patch/upgrade or configuration rollout.
- Does NOT cover: customer-managed external dependencies (e.g., third-party DBs) except where Redwood config changes interact directly.

Preconditions (must-check before any planned upgrade):
1) Backups & snapshots: confirm last full control-plane snapshot is completed and stored in the configured customer bucket. Snapshot timestamp: <ISO timestamp>.
2) Health baseline: capture baseline metrics for 15 min prior to change (latency p95, CPU/GPU utilization, request success rate, cache hit rate). Attach reports to the change ticket.
3) Canary capacity: allocate a canary pool with isolated routing (>=1% traffic and at least N concurrent sessions, where N = max(10, 0.01 * expected concurrent load)).
4) Rollback playbook verified: owners and on-call contact listed in the change ticket.

Key failure-isolation patterns (design rules):
- Traffic fencing: use route-level flags and feature gates so new binaries/configs can be routed only from an explicit routing table entry.
- Config gating: store critical rollout knobs in the control-plane feature collection; changes to these keys must be reversible and have a TTL.
- Immutable artifacts: build deterministic artifacts (sha256). If artifact mismatch occurs, auto-reject rollout.
- Gradual widening: 0 -> canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated health gates at each step.

Decision criteria for rollback (one or more triggers):
- Latency: sustained p95 increase > 2x baseline for 5 minutes.
- Errors: request error rate increase > 1% absolute and >= 3x baseline for 3 minutes.
- Throughput degradation: end-to-end throughput drop > 20% for 5 minutes with no external cause.
- Resource saturation: any node with GPU memory OOM, kernel panic, repeated process restarts (>3 restarts in 5 minutes).
- Security regression: any failing auth or encryption checks during/after rollout.

Recommended manual rollback procedure (control-plane or runtime service):
1) Triage and verify: confirm metrics trigger was real (check Prometheus, traces, and node logs). Record decision in the incident/change ticket.
2) Stop new widening: set rollout flag to paused.
3) Shift traffic: route 100% traffic away from canary/widened group to last-known-good pool. Use routing command: 
   rwd-router set-route --deployment <DEPLOYMENT_ID> --target-pool <GOOD_POOL_ID> --drain-time 30s
4) If traffic cannot be re-routed cleanly, place a temporary denylist for new sessions at the gateway: 
   rwd-gateway denylist add --match "session=new" --reason "rollback in progress"
5) Revert artifacts: pin model/runtime to previous artifact SHA. Example pin file (used by control-plane):

   pinned_artifact: >
     deployment: infra-runtime
     version: 2026.01.14
     sha256: abcd1234ef567890...

   Apply revert command: rwd-deploy rollback --deployment infra-runtime --to-sha abcd1234ef567890 --force

6) Rollback config: restore previous config bundle from snapshot store. Example restore: rwd-config restore --snapshot-id snap-20260210-2145 --components control-plane,runtime
7) Verify service health: follow verification checklist below.
8) Close ticket with a post-rollback summary including root cause hypothesis and actions to mitigate in next rollout.

Automated rollback choreography (when health gates are enabled):
- Health gate engine monitors: p95 latency, error rate, GPU OOM rate, and control-plane heartbeat.
- If any configured gate trips, the system will attempt: 1) pause widen, 2) move traffic back to the last good pool, 3) notify on-call channel, 4) if critical triggers persist for 90s, automatically initiate artifact revert.
- To disable automated rollback for a specific rollout, add hold tag: rollout.hold=true in the change request (not recommended unless supervised).

Verification checklist (post-rollback):
- Control-plane: api-server 200s check, queue depth stable, config hash matches pinned SHA.
- Runtime: no GPU OOMs for 30 minutes, tail latency p50/p95 within 15% of baseline.
- Workloads: 10 synthetic requests per model class succeed end-to-end, embeddings within expected vector L2 tolerance.
- Logs: no new error patterns (>5 occurrences) in last 15 minutes.
- Security: TLS session negotiation passes, KMS sign/verify checks succeed.

Concrete commands and examples (CLI snippets):
- Snapshot control plane:
  rwd-control snapshot create --name pre-upgrade-2026-02-12

- Create canary pool (example YAML passed to control-plane API):
  ```yaml
  kind: Pool
  name: canary-2026-02-12
  labels:
    purpose: canary
    owner: eng-platform
  size: 4
  allowed_models: [rwd-gpt-small, rwd-gpt-medium]
  ```

- Trigger manual rollback for runtime:
  rwd-deploy rollback --deployment inference-runtime --reason "p95 spike" --to-tag last-good

- Inspect recent errors (Kubernetes example):
  kubectl -n rwd-runtime logs deployment/inference-runtime --since=15m | grep -i error | head -n 200

Operational notes and edge cases:
- Database schema incompatible migrations: never auto-rollback schema changes. For schema rollouts, use migration gating and a multi-step backward-compatible migration plan. If a schema incompatibility is detected, trigger service-level rollback but coordinate with DBA team to run the corrective migration.
- Persistent data corruption suspected: isolate affected nodes immediately, take disk snapshots, and contact Security for potential forensics. Do NOT reintroduce those nodes into the pool.
- Multi-region fallbacks: if local region capacity causes rollback, prefer moving traffic to a warm spare region with identical model versions. Ensure legal/data-residency approvals before cross-region movement.

Post-incident actions and ownership:
- Postmortem owner: on-call engineer who initiated rollback (or explicit postmortem owner in ticket).
- RCA timeline: initial report due within 2 business days, full RCA with action items within 7 business days.
- Preventative controls: implement additional health gates, add synthetic tests, or modify resource requests based on root cause.

Compatibility and upgrade matrix (excerpt):
- Control plane version 2025.12.x: compatible with runtime 2025.10.x -> 2026.01.x (recommended).
- Runtime GPU driver: NVIDIA 535.x required for 16-bit quantized kernels.
- KV cache format v2 requires control-plane >=2026.01.

Safety checklist before re-attempting rollout:
1) Confirm root cause has been mitigated or a compensating control exists.
2) Increase canary pool size by 2x and reduce widening step to 5% increments.
3) Add extra synthetic probes and extend observation window to 30 minutes between steps.
4) Ensure on-call rotation for the next 48 hours has explicit coverage.

Troubleshooting quick reference (common scenarios):
- Symptom: p95 doubled immediately after rollout. Check: network egress throttling on gateway, routing misconfiguration, and runtime CPU throttling. Action: move traffic and revert.
- Symptom: GPU OOM on new model. Check: model quantization profile, batch size defaults. Action: rollback to previous model; file model-onboarding ticket.

Appendix A — Minimal set of monitoring queries to attach to the change ticket:
- PromQL p95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[1m])) by (le, route))
- Error rate: sum(rate(request_errors_total[1m])) / sum(rate(request_total[1m]))
- Node restarts: increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total[5m]) > 0

Appendix B — Contact & escalation matrix:
- Primary on-call (Platform SRE): pager duty rotation rwd-platform-pager (escalate after 5 min)
- Control-plane owner: eng-platform@redwood.example.com
- Security: sec-ops@redwood.example.com (for suspected compromise)

Document maintenance:
- Owner: eng-platform
- Review cadence: quarterly or after any major rollback incident
- Last reviewed by: Marco Perez on 2026-03-01

Related artifacts and links:
- Pre-rollout checklist template: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/templates/pre-rollout-checklist
- Canary dashboard: /dashboards/canary-health

End of document.",

    "content": "{\n  \"thread_id\": \"thread-20280809-borealis-34219\",\n  \"mailbox_owner\": \"olga_petrov\",\n  \"subject\": \"Borealis Health \\u2014 private deployment onboarding: network evidence & next steps\",\n  \"participants_internal\": [\n    \"olga_petrov\",\n    \"ben_carter\",\n    \"kimberly_park\",\n    \"vivek_kulkarni\"\n  ],\n  \"participants_external\": [\n    \"Paul Nguyen <paul@borealishealth.com>\",\n    \"TechOps Team <techops@borealishealth.com>\",\n    \"Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@borealishealth.com>\"\n  ],\n  \"message_count\": \"5\",\n  \"first_email_at\": \"2028-08-01T09:12:00-07:00\",\n  \"last_email_at\": \"2028-08-09T16:45:00-07:00\",\n  \"thread_type\": \"security_compliance\",\n  \"related_account\": \"Borealis Health\",\n  \"deal_id\": \"DEAL-34219\",\n  \"region\": \"us\",\n  \"has_attachments\": \"true\",\n  \"attachments\": [\n    \"borealis-network-diagram-v2.pdf\",\n    \"kms-integration-reqs.xlsx\",\n    \"redwood-onboard-map.txt\"\n  ],\n  \"related_links\": [\n    \"https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBorealisOnboardEvidence\",\n    \"https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/34219/company/7182\",\n    \"https://docusign.com/tx/DEAL-34219/onboard-agreement\"\n  ],\n  \"messages\": [\n    \"From: Paul Nguyen <paul@borealishealth.com>\\nTo: olga_petrov@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com\\nCc: TechOps Team <techops@borealishealth.com>\\nDate: Tue, 01 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700\\nSubject: Private deployment intake \\u2014 network evidence & KMS questions\\n\\nHi Olga / Ben,\\n\\nThanks again for the walkthrough earlier. We want to keep momentum on getting our private deployment scheduled for the week of Aug 21. To make sure our security/compliance team has what they need, can you confirm the minimal network artifacts Redwood requires to validate the environment? Specific asks from our side: \\n\\n- A sample service account principle and required IAM roles for the provisioning step\\n- KMS integration checklist (customer KMS vs Redwood-managed keys)\\n- Firewall port list and egress destinations your installers talk to during provisioning\\n- Any required DNS records or SRV entries for telemetry/health checks\\n\\nI'll attach our current network diagram and we can map gaps on your side. If you can outline a short mutual action plan (MAP) we can circulate to our security reviewers.\\n\\nAppreciate it \\u2014 Paul\\n\\n--\\nPaul Nguyen\\nDirector, Infrastructure \\u2014 Borealis Health\\npaul@borealishealth.com\\n+1 (415) 555-0134\\n\",\n    \"From: olga_petrov@redwood.com <olga_petrov@redwood.com>\\nTo: Paul Nguyen <paul@borealishealth.com>\\nCc: ben_carter@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com\\nDate: Wed, 02 Aug 2028 11:38:00 -0700\\nSubject: Re: Private deployment intake \\u2014 network evidence & KMS questions\\n\\nPaul \\u2014\\n\\nThanks for the clear list. Below is the short intake summary and the minimal evidence items we need to complete pre-provisioning validation. I've listed ownership for each item so we have clear owners for the MAP: \\n\\n1) IAM/service accounts (owner: Borealis)\\n   - Service account used for deployment with roles: ComputeAdmin (provisioner), KMSCryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter (if using customer KMS), StorageObjectAdmin (artifact staging).\\n   - Evidence: service-account JSON (or equivalent role binding screenshots) + policy doc.\\n\\n2) KMS choices (owner: joint)\\n   - Option A: Customer-managed KMS (recommended for regulated workloads). We need key ARN/ID and admin contact.\\n   - Option B: Redwood-managed keys (simpler \\u2014 will require data-at-rest attestation).\\n   - Evidence: key policy snippet + rotation window.\\n\\n3) Network & firewall (owner: Borealis)\\n   - Required egress to: api.redwood-inference.com (443), 52.23.*/18 (provisioning pool CIDR), monitoring.redwood-inference.com (443).\\n   - Ports: 443 outbound, 22 inbound (optional, jumpbox), NTP 123 UDP to pool NTP servers if locked down.\\n   - Evidence: FW rule exports (CSV) and VPC peering/route table exports.\\n\\n4) DNS & TLS (owner: Borealis)\\n   - We require CNAMEs for service discovery only if customer-managed hostnames are desired. TLS certs can be customer-provided or Redwood-provisioned via ACME.\\n\\n5) Telemetry & audit (owner: joint)\\n   - Audit log forwarding endpoints and retention window.\\n\\nNext steps (proposed MAP):\\n- Aug 03: Borealis provides network diagram + service account role export (Paul)\\n- Aug 06: Redwood reviews diagram, returns annotated diagram + gap list (Olga)\\n- Aug 09: Borealis returns KMS policy and FW rule exports; Redwood confirms final checklist (Ben)\\n- Aug 11: Pre-provisioning signoff and scheduling\\n\\nI attached a short template you can paste into your internal ticketing to accelerate evidence collection.\\n\\nRegards,\\nOlga\\n\\n--\\nOlga Petrov\\nTechnical Program Manager, Private Deployments\\nRedwood Inference\\nolga_petrov@redwood.com\\n[attachment: redwood-onboard-map.txt]\",\n    \"From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@borealishealth.com>\\nTo: olga_petrov@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com\\nCc: Paul Nguyen <paul@borealishealth.com>, TechOps Team <techops@borealishealth.com>\\nDate: Fri, 04 Aug 2028 14:22:00 -0700\\nSubject: Re: Private deployment intake \\u2014 network evidence & KMS questions\\n\\nThanks Olga \\u2014 attaching our updated network diagram and a KMS excerpt. See attachments: borealis-network-diagram-v2.pdf and kms-integration-reqs.xlsx.\\n\\nA couple clarifications:\\n- Our security team prefers customer-managed KMS; I'll include the key admin contact in a follow-up (they're out today).\\n- We will export firewall rules from the next maintenance window (Aug 05) and upload the CSV to the Drive folder you shared.\\n\\nOn the service account: do you need the raw JSON key file or just role binding screenshots? Security baseline here prefers role-binding screenshots only.\\n\\nThanks \\u2014 Samantha\\n\\n--\\nSamantha Ortiz\\nSr. Cloud Engineer \\u2014 Borealis Health\\nsamantha.ortiz@borealishealth.com\\n[attachment: borealis-network-diagram-v2.pdf] [attachment: kms-integration-reqs.xlsx]\",\n    \"From: ben_carter@redwood.com <ben_carter@redwood.com>\\nTo: olga_petrov@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com\\nCc: Paul Nguyen <paul@borealishealth.com>, samantha.ortiz@borealishealth.com\\nDate: Mon, 07 Aug 2028 10:09:00 -0700\\nSubject: Re: Private deployment intake \\u2014 network evidence & KMS questions\\n\\nQuick notes after reviewing the diagram and KMS sheet: \\n\\n- Diagram looks good; there's a missing route for the provisioning pool CIDR in the east-az subnet (Samantha \\u2014 can you confirm route table export includes the 10.121.0.0/16 route?).\\n- On service account evidence: we can accept role-binding screenshots and a short statement from your security owner confirming no long-lived keys are present. We will not ask for raw key JSON over email.\\n- For KMS: if customer-managed, we need a key policy snippet showing Redwoods' service principal has Encrypt/Decrypt permissions. A single redacted snippet is sufficient.\\n\\nI'll prepare an annotated diagram with the provisioning endpoints highlighted and upload it to the Drive folder by EOD. Once we have the firewall CSV and the route table export, we can mark \\\"network validated\\\" and book provisioning.\\n\\nBen\\n\\n--\\nBen Carter\\nOnboarding Lead, Private Deploys\\nRedwood Inference\\n[attachment: borealis-network-diagram-annotated.pdf]\",\n    \"From: olga_petrov@redwood.com <olga_petrov@redwood.com>\\nTo: Paul Nguyen <paul@borealishealth.com>, Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@borealishealth.com>\\nCc: ben_carter@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com\\nDate: Tue, 09 Aug 2028 16:45:00 -0700\\nSubject: Re: Private deployment intake \\u2014 network evidence & KMS questions\\n\\nThanks team \\u2014 short confirmation and next-actions.\\n\\n1) Borealis to upload FW CSV + route-table export into Drive by 08-10 (Paul / Samantha)\\n2) Borealis to paste KMS policy snippet (redacted) into the Drive folder by 08-10; Redwood will verify permissions (Vivek)\\n3) Redwood will present the final annotated diagram and the provisioning window options by 08-11 (Ben)\\n\\nIf all items above land on 08-10 and verification completes, we are tentatively green for provisioning the week of Aug 21. I will open the calendar hold for a half-day provisioning window and share the invite once Ben confirms the exact times.\\n\\nQuick ask for your security reviewer: please confirm whether SRV records are locked to internal DNS \\u2014 if so, that will change our onboarding checklist slightly (we require either a temporary split-horizon DNS entry or explicit host mappings).\\n\\nOlga\\n\\n--\\nOlga Petrov\\nTechnical Program Manager, Private Deployments\\nRedwood Inference\\nolga_petrov@redwood.com\\n[attachment: borealis-network-diagram-annotated.pdf]\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"subject\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"messages\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_91f68bedf2d0467ab757b8bc6990d4c0\"\n}",

document.title: Borealis Health — private deployment onboarding: network evidence & next steps
document.content:
{
  "thread_id": "thread-20280809-borealis-34219",
  "mailbox_owner": "olga_petrov",
  "subject": "Borealis Health — private deployment onboarding: network evidence & next steps",
  "participants_internal": [
    "olga_petrov",
    "ben_carter",
    "kimberly_park",
    "vivek_kulkarni"
  ],
  "participants_external": [
    "Paul Nguyen <paul@borealishealth.com>",
    "TechOps Team <techops@borealishealth.com>",
    "Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@borealishealth.com>"
  ],
  "message_count": "5",
  "first_email_at": "2028-08-01T09:12:00-07:00",
  "last_email_at": "2028-08-09T16:45:00-07:00",
  "thread_type": "security_compliance",
  "related_account": "Borealis Health",
  "deal_id": "DEAL-34219",
  "region": "us",
  "has_attachments": "true",
  "attachments": [
    "borealis-network-diagram-v2.pdf",
    "kms-integration-reqs.xlsx",
    "redwood-onboard-map.txt"
  ],
  "related_links": [
    "https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBorealisOnboardEvidence",
    "https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/34219/company/7182",
    "https://docusign.com/tx/DEAL-34219/onboard-agreement"
  ],
  "messages": [
    "From: Paul Nguyen <paul@borealishealth.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: TechOps Team <techops@borealishealth.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment intake — network evidence & KMS questions

Hi Olga / Ben,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. We want to keep momentum on getting our private deployment scheduled for the week of Aug 21. To make sure our security/compliance team has what they need, can you confirm the minimal network artifacts Redwood requires to validate the environment? Specific asks from our side: 

- A sample service account principle and required IAM roles for the provisioning step
- KMS integration checklist (customer KMS vs Redwood-managed keys)
- Firewall port list and egress destinations your installers talk to during provisioning
- Any required DNS records or SRV entries for telemetry/health checks

I'll attach our current network diagram and we can map gaps on your side. If you can outline a short mutual action plan (MAP) we can circulate to our security reviewers.

Appreciate it — Paul

--
Paul Nguyen
Director, Infrastructure — Borealis Health
paul@borealishealth.com
+1 (415) 555-0134
",
    "From: olga_petrov@redwood.com <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Paul Nguyen <paul@borealishealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 02 Aug 2028 11:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment intake — network evidence & KMS questions

Paul —

Thanks for the clear list. Below is the short intake summary and the minimal evidence items we need to complete pre-provisioning validation. I've listed ownership for each item so we have clear owners for the MAP: 

1) IAM/service accounts (owner: Borealis)
   - Service account used for deployment with roles: ComputeAdmin (provisioner), KMSCryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter (if using customer KMS), StorageObjectAdmin (artifact staging).
   - Evidence: service-account JSON (or equivalent role binding screenshots) + policy doc.

2) KMS choices (owner: joint)
   - Option A: Customer-managed KMS (recommended for regulated workloads). We need key ARN/ID and admin contact.
   - Option B: Redwood-managed keys (simpler — will require data-at-rest attestation).
   - Evidence: key policy snippet + rotation window.

3) Network & firewall (owner: Borealis)
   - Required egress to: api.redwood-inference.com (443), 52.23.*/18 (provisioning pool CIDR), monitoring.redwood-inference.com (443).
   - Ports: 443 outbound, 22 inbound (optional, jumpbox), NTP 123 UDP to pool NTP servers if locked down.
   - Evidence: FW rule exports (CSV) and VPC peering/route table exports.

4) DNS & TLS (owner: Borealis)
   - We require CNAMEs for service discovery only if customer-managed hostnames are desired. TLS certs can be customer-provided or Redwood-provisioned via ACME.

5) Telemetry & audit (owner: joint)
   - Audit log forwarding endpoints and retention window.

Next steps (proposed MAP):
- Aug 03: Borealis provides network diagram + service account role export (Paul)
- Aug 06: Redwood reviews diagram, returns annotated diagram + gap list (Olga)
- Aug 09: Borealis returns KMS policy and FW rule exports; Redwood confirms final checklist (Ben)
- Aug 11: Pre-provisioning signoff and scheduling

I attached a short template you can paste into your internal ticketing to accelerate evidence collection.

Regards,
Olga

--
Olga Petrov
Technical Program Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com
[attachment: redwood-onboard-map.txt]",
    "From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@borealishealth.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Paul Nguyen <paul@borealishealth.com>, TechOps Team <techops@borealishealth.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Aug 2028 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment intake — network evidence & KMS questions

Thanks Olga — attaching our updated network diagram and a KMS excerpt. See attachments: borealis-network-diagram-v2.pdf and kms-integration-reqs.xlsx.

A couple clarifications:
- Our security team prefers customer-managed KMS; I'll include the key admin contact in a follow-up (they're out today).
- We will export firewall rules from the next maintenance window (Aug 05) and upload the CSV to the Drive folder you shared.

On the service account: do you need the raw JSON key file or just role binding screenshots? Security baseline here prefers role-binding screenshots only.

Thanks — Samantha

--
Samantha Ortiz
Sr. Cloud Engineer — Borealis Health
samantha.ortiz@borealishealth.com
[attachment: borealis-network-diagram-v2.pdf] [attachment: kms-integration-reqs.xlsx]",
    "From: ben_carter@redwood.com <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: Paul Nguyen <paul@borealishealth.com>, samantha.ortiz@borealishealth.com
Date: Mon, 07 Aug 2028 10:09:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment intake — network evidence & KMS questions

Quick notes after reviewing the diagram and KMS sheet: 

- Diagram looks good; there's a missing route for the provisioning pool CIDR in the east-az subnet (Samantha — can you confirm route table export includes the 10.121.0.0/16 route?).
- On service account evidence: we can accept role-binding screenshots and a short statement from your security owner confirming no long-lived keys are present. We will not ask for raw key JSON over email.
- For KMS: if customer-managed, we need a key policy snippet showing Redwoods' service principal has Encrypt/Decrypt permissions. A single redacted snippet is sufficient.

I'll prepare an annotated diagram with the provisioning endpoints highlighted and upload it to the Drive folder by EOD. Once we have the firewall CSV and the route table export, we can mark "network validated" and book provisioning.

Ben

--
Ben Carter
Onboarding Lead, Private Deploys
Redwood Inference
[attachment: borealis-network-diagram-annotated.pdf]",
    "From: olga_petrov@redwood.com <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Paul Nguyen <paul@borealishealth.com>, Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@borealishealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 09 Aug 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment intake — network evidence & KMS questions

Thanks team — short confirmation and next-actions.

1) Borealis to upload FW CSV + route-table export into Drive by 08-10 (Paul / Samantha)
2) Borealis to paste KMS policy snippet (redacted) into the Drive folder by 08-10; Redwood will verify permissions (Vivek)
3) Redwood will present the final annotated diagram and the provisioning window options by 08-11 (Ben)

If all items above land on 08-10 and verification completes, we are tentatively green for provisioning the week of Aug 21. I will open the calendar hold for a half-day provisioning window and share the invite once Ben confirms the exact times.

Quick ask for your security reviewer: please confirm whether SRV records are locked to internal DNS — if so, that will change our onboarding checklist slightly (we require either a temporary split-horizon DNS entry or explicit host mappings).

Olga

--
Olga Petrov
Technical Program Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com

    "content": "{\n  \"thread_id\": \"kp-20270322-upgrade-001\",\n  \"mailbox_owner\": \"kimberly_park\",\n  \"subject\": \"Private deployment: upgrade comms, phased rollout & rollback matrix\",\n  \"participants_internal\": [\n    \"kimberly_park\",\n    \"mateo_alvarez\",\n    \"karthik_iyer\",\n    \"neha_kapoor\",\n    \"dylan_brooks\"\n  ],\n  \"participants_external\": [\n    \"Cameron Blake <cameron@acmecloud.com>\",\n    \"BigBank SecOps <audits@bigbank.com>\"\n  ],\n  \"message_count\": \"5\",\n  \"first_email_at\": \"2027-03-22T09:14:00-07:00\",\n  \"last_email_at\": \"2027-03-23T11:05:00-07:00\",\n  \"thread_type\": \"security_compliance\",\n  \"related_account\": \"BigBank Corp\",\n  \"region\": \"us\",\n  \"has_attachments\": \"true\",\n  \"attachments\": [\n    \"upgrade_matrix_v2.xlsx\",\n    \"comm_plan_draft.md\",\n    \"acme_vpc_routes.png\"\n  ],\n  \"related_links\": [\n    \"https://calendar.redwood.com/event/3b9f-upgrade-window\",\n    \"https://docs.redwood.com/private/upgrade-runbook-v2\"\n  ],\n  \"messages\": [\n    \"From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>\\\\nTo: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>\\\\nCc: Cameron Blake <cameron@acmecloud.com>\\\\nDate: 2027-03-22T09:14:00-07:00\\\\nSubject: Private deployment: upgrade comms, phased rollout & rollback matrix\\\\n\\\\nTeam \\u2014\\\\n\\\\nPer BigBank's request we need to schedule the next Private runtime patch (v3.2.1 -> v3.3.0) for their on-prem/VPC deployment and lock down a clear communications and rollback plan. Draft attached: \\\\\\\"upgrade_matrix_v2.xlsx\\\\\\\" + a short comms draft in \\\\\\\"comm_plan_draft.md\\\\\\\". High-level asks below so we can finalize before Friday: \\\\n\\\\n- Proposed maintenance window: Sat Mar 27 01:00\\u201305:00 PT (4h) with a 1h canary phase followed by bulk cutover.\\\\n- Version pinning: customer currently pinned to 3.2.1; we will propose a soft pin to 3.3.0 for 30 days post-upgrade, with automatic fallback to 3.2.1 if health signals fail.\\\\n- Rollback criteria (initial): CPU/GPU mem > 85% sustained for 10m, p99 latency degradation > 40%, error rate increase > 3x baseline, or failed KV cache warmup after canary.\\\\n- Network changes: small route table change to support new sidecar metrics; CAM needs to confirm no IP conflicts.\\\\n- Audit/compliance: ensure audit logs for config changes and a KMS key rotation window is scheduled with Neha.\\\\n\\\\nPlease review the matrix and suggest edits inline. Specific asks: \\\\n  * Mateo \\u2014 confirm canary cluster size and gate thresholds.\\\\n  * Karthik \\u2014 ops orchestration steps and any preflight health checks we should add.\\\\n  * Neha \\u2014 compliance gating and evidence we must provide to BigBank.\\\\n  * Dylan \\u2014 runbook owner for rollback; include checklist for snapshot/restore.\\\\n\\\\nIf we agree on Sat 27, I'll send the official notice to BigBank and schedule the 01:00 calendar invite.\\\\n\\\\nThanks,\\\\nKimberly\\\\n\\\\n--\\\\nKimberly Park\\\\nSenior Program Manager, Private Deployments\\\\nRedwood Inference\\\\n\",\n    \"From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>\\\\nTo: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>\\\\nCc: Cameron Blake <cameron@acmecloud.com>\\\\nDate: 2027-03-22T10:03:00-07:00\\\\nSubject: Re: Private deployment: upgrade comms, phased rollout & rollback matrix\\\\n\\\\nKimberly \\u2014 quick read through the matrix. A few notes: \\\\n\\\\n1) Canary sizing: recommend 10% of production capacity or a minimum of 2 GPU nodes (whichever is higher) for 60m. That gives us prefix/KV cache warmup observation without fully exposing all traffic.\\\\n2) Gate thresholds: add a third gate for model-level token divergence (automated prompt smoke tests) \\u2014 if generation quality drops by > 8% on our golden prompts, fail canary.\\\\n3) Snapshot cadence: ensure we take both L0 (VM) and model checkpoint snapshots pre-cutover. If snapshot+restore time > 45m for BigBank infra, schedule extra buffer.\\\\n\\\\nAlso suggest adding a nightly preflight run for three nights prior to the window to validate images and sidecar versions on a staging clone. I'll update the workbook with canary numbers.\\\\n\\\\nOn the rollback approach: prefer a staged rollback (canary -> region -> full) rather than full immediate revert unless critical. Dylan, can you confirm the rollback playbook includes automatic drain and token blackhole steps?\\\\n\\\\nMateo\\\\nPrincipal Site Reliability Engineer\\\\n\",\n    \"From: Cameron Blake <cameron@acmecloud.com>\\\\nTo: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>\\\\nDate: 2027-03-22T13:21:00-07:00\\\\nSubject: Re: Private deployment: upgrade comms, phased rollout & rollback matrix\\\\n\\\\nThanks for the heads up, Kimberly. A couple of constraints from our side (BigBank's VPC team):\\\\n\\\\n- Blackout windows: BigBank has a regulatory blackout from 02:30\\u201303:30 PT on Sat due to overnight batch jobs; we cannot touch routes or IPs during that hour. That conflicts with the current canary window.\\\\n- IP whitelisting: after upgrade the sidecar metrics endpoint will originate from a new ephemeral IP range (10.200.5.0/24). Need confirmation we can add that to their VPC ACLs and firewall rules at least 24h in advance.\\\\n- Network diagram attached: \\\\\\\"acme_vpc_routes.png\\\\\\\" \\u2014 please verify the proposed route change won't overlap the DB migration VLAN.\\\\n\\\\nIf we must move the canary earlier, we can do 00:15\\u201301:15 PT for canary and bulk after the blackout, but that compresses the lead time for rollback.\\\\n\\\\nCameron\\\\nIntegration Lead, ACME Cloud Services\\\\n\",\n    \"From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>\\\\nTo: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>\\\\nCc: Cameron Blake <cameron@acmecloud.com>\\\\nDate: 2027-03-22T17:46:00-07:00\\\\nSubject: Re: Private deployment: upgrade comms, phased rollout & rollback matrix\\\\n\\\\nCouple of compliance/controls items we'll need to bake in before sending the official notice to BigBank: \\\\n\\\\n- Audit trail: all config changes and deployment steps must be pushed to the customer's audit S3 bucket (or provided via secure share) within 2 hours of completion. Add step in runbook to capture run-level logs and signed manifests.\\\\n- KMS rotation: do not schedule a KMS rotation inside the 30-day soft-pin window. If BigBank wants a rotation, schedule it 48h before the upgrade or 30 days after.\\\\n- Evidence pack: BigBank will request pre/post snapshots and syscall-level audit logs for the canary hosts. Prepare a redacted evidence pack template we can drop into DocShare.\\\\n- Fallback policy: strongly prefer an automated graceful traffic shift to hosted fallback for 30\\u2013120m during rollback if their infra allows it. If not possible, ensure we have a documented manual fallback and escalation path.\\\\n\\\\nI'll attach the evidence checklist to the workbook and mark the gating items.\\\\n\\\\nNeha\\\\nSecurity & Compliance Lead\\\\n\",\n    \"From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>\\\\nTo: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>\\\\nCc: Cameron Blake <cameron@acmecloud.com>, BigBank SecOps <audits@bigbank.com>\\\\nDate: 2027-03-23T11:05:00-07:00\\\\nSubject: Re: Private deployment: upgrade comms, phased rollout & rollback matrix\\\\n\\\\nThanks all \\u2014 consolidated next steps below and decisions so we can lock the notice.\\\\n\\\\nDecisions: \\\\n- Maintenance window: Sat Mar 27 00:15\\u201305:00 PT. Canary 00:15\\u201301:15, blackout 02:30\\u201303:30 (no route changes), bulk cutover after 03:30.\\\\n- Version pin: 3.3.0 soft-pin for 30 days; automatic rollback to 3.2.1 if any of the primary gates trip.\\\\n- Rollback approach: staged rollback (canary -> region -> full) unless critical failure; add hosted fallback as preferred option if customer consents.\\\\n\\\\nAction owners: \\\\n- Mateo: update matrix with canary node counts, add golden-prompt smoke tests (due 2027-03-24 12:00 PT).\\\\n- Karthik: finalize orchestration steps, preflight checklist, and snapshot run times (due 2027-03-24 18:00 PT).\\\\n- Neha: finalize evidence pack template and list of logs to push to BigBank (due 2027-03-24 15:00 PT).\\\\n- Dylan: publish rollback playbook with drain/blackhole commands and time estimates (due 2027-03-24 20:00 PT).\\\\n- Cameron / ACME: confirm IP whitelist change timing and approve route diagram (please respond by 2027-03-23 17:00 PT).\\\\n\\\\nI'll incorporate all updates into the workbook and send the customer-facing maintenance notice after we have the items above. Calendar invite + runbook link will follow.\\\\n\\\\nAttachments: upgrade_matrix_v2.xlsx, comm_plan_draft.md, acme_vpc_routes.png\\\\n\\\\nKimberly\\\\nSenior Program Manager, Private Deployments\\\\nRedwood Inference\\\\n\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"subject\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"messages\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_a43a83f1a6744c2fb07b1583f14c86c4\"\n}",
